paper.title: DAPPER Correlation and Survival (capsule 3894632; capsule README + stored results used as paper text)

claims.text: Radiomic, microbiome and clinical features are correlated with one another in the DAPPER LMS cohort; the correlation spreadsheet can be sorted by strength, significance and correlation type.
A reduced feature set derived from the correlation analysis is the input to the survival analysis.
Univariate Cox models for PFS identify clinical features (best RECIST response, Gr1/Gr2 toxicities, Gr3 toxicities) as associated with PFS after FDR adjustment.
No radiomic principal component is significantly associated with PFS (all p.adjust > 0.68).
No microbiome feature (Shannon diversity or species relative abundance) is significantly associated with PFS (all p.adjust > 0.68).
The same univariate Cox pipeline is applied to overall survival (OS) and produces a second results data frame.
Features are mean/sd normalized before modelling and p-values are FDR-adjusted across all tested features.

findings.evidence: No dependency specification found (requirements.txt, environment.yml, renv.lock, ...).
findings.question_for_authors: Which software and library versions were used?

findings.evidence: [G4] Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)? -> not_reported. No outlier definition or removal rule is stated.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)?

findings.evidence: [M1] Are random seeds stated, and are results reported over several seeds? -> not_reported. No random seed; PCA sign convention not stated.
findings.question_for_authors: Are random seeds stated, and are results reported over several seeds?

findings.evidence: [M10] If the paper credits specific features or descriptors for the performance, is there a negative control (random or shuffled features, one-hot identity encoding, y-randomisation)? -> not_reported. No negative control (e.g. permuted outcome) for the radiomic/microbiome features.
findings.question_for_authors: Was any negative control (permuted outcome or shuffled features) run for the radiomic and microbiome screens?

findings.evidence: The R notebook drops the first two columns of reduced-feature-set.csv (index column and 'Age') from the covariate list, so Age is never tested; the stored table has 39 rows for 41 candidate columns.
findings.question_for_authors: Was Age intentionally excluded from the univariate Cox models, and why?

findings.evidence: FDR adjustment is applied over the 39 univariate tests only. The same capsule also runs 819 pairwise correlation tests (results/correlation_results.csv) on the same 30 subjects, and the reduced feature set is chosen from that screen before the survival models are fitted.
findings.question_for_authors: Should the FDR family include the 819 correlation tests that selected the features entering the survival models?

findings.evidence: Best response (RECIST) and toxicity grades are post-baseline, on-treatment variables, yet they are entered as baseline covariates in univariate Cox models of PFS (PFS_time_RECISTv1).
findings.question_for_authors: Were response and toxicity measured before the PFS event time in every subject (landmark analysis), or can the association be partly tautological?

findings.evidence: README says the correlation spreadsheet can be sorted by 'correlation type (e.g., correlation between imaging feature and microbiome feature versus microbiome-microbiome)', but functionals.py computes one pooled matrix and writes a single 'r-Value' column without a correlation-type label.
findings.question_for_authors: Which column of correlation_results.csv encodes the correlation type described in the README?

findings.location: bp_out/multiverse_results.csv (15 evaluable universes of a 36-universe grid)
findings.evidence: Baseline (authors' choices: covariates without Age, BH-FDR, no outlier rule, post-baseline covariates kept) holds: padj Best.Response=0.0215, padj Gr3=0.0215, min padj radiomic=0.747. The claim holds in 8/15 evaluable universes (53%). Breaking changes: dropping subjects with |z|>3 on any continuous feature raises padj Best.Response/Gr3 to 0.059 (fails); Bonferroni instead of BH also fails at |z|>3 (0.119/0.098); with no correction and |z|>2.5 the minimum radiomic padj falls to 0.010, so a radiomic component becomes nominally significant. The 12 universes with post_baseline=drop are not evaluable because they remove the two features the claim is about.
findings.question_for_authors: How sensitive are the two FDR-significant PFS associations to the exclusion of a single influential subject and to the choice of correction?

findings.evidence: Our re-computation of 'p.adjust Best.Response.RECISTv1 (PFS)' gives 0.022 (bp_work/code/port/cox_port.py), but the authors' stored output (results/dp_survival.nb.html) gives 0.02145; the stored output agrees with the paper, so this is our port's problem, not a paper finding.
Our re-computation of 'p.adjust Gr3.Toxicities (PFS)' gives 0.022, the authors' stored output gives 0.02145; stored output agrees with the paper.
Our re-computation of 'p.adjust Gr1.Gr2.Toxicities (PFS)' gives 0.9991, the authors' stored output gives 0.0377; stored output agrees with the paper, so the discrepancy is in our lifelines port.
Our re-computation of 'p.adjust Component.2 (PFS)' gives 0.7022, the authors' stored output gives 0.6825; stored output agrees with the paper.

findings.location: bp_work/code/port/cox_port.py (covariates after R's covariates[-1]) vs results/dp_survival.nb.html
findings.evidence: Our re-computation of 'n features tested (PFS)' gives 40, the authors' stored output gives 39; stored output agrees with the paper.
2 data-exclusion step(s): dropna@100, dropna@101. Candidate forks for the multiverse stage.
findings.question_for_authors: How many subjects are removed by the dropna steps, and were they removed before or after feature selection?

findings.evidence: [G1] Is the exact data source identified (version, DOI, accession, download date)? -> partial. Capsule data are the DAPPER trial data; no version/DOI/accession is given.
findings.question_for_authors: Which data version/accession underlies the capsule tables?

findings.evidence: [G2] Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step? -> partial. 30 subjects enter the analysis; the exclusion steps from the trial cohort to these 30 are not reported.
findings.question_for_authors: How many DAPPER patients were excluded before the 30 analysed subjects, and why?

findings.evidence: [G5] Is the sample size justified (power analysis or other rationale)? -> not_reported. No power analysis; n=30 with 28 PFS events and 39-40 tests.
findings.question_for_authors: What detectable hazard ratio does n=30 with 28 PFS events give after FDR correction?

findings.evidence: README states the survival notebook 'generates two dataframes' for OS and PFS, and code/dp_survival.Rmd contains an OS chunk, but the stored notebook output contains only the PFS table.
findings.question_for_authors: Where is the OS results table, and what does it show?

findings.evidence: All univariate models use 30 subjects (28 PFS events, 13 OS events) and 39-40 covariates are tested; the capsule reports no power calculation, no confidence-interval method and no proportional-hazards check.
findings.question_for_authors: Were proportional-hazards assumptions checked for the two significant PFS models?

findings.evidence: The correlation matrix mixes Cramer's V (categorical-categorical), point-biserial (mixed) and Pearson/Spearman coefficients in one 'r-Value' column and one p-value column, so the 819 tests are not on a common scale.
findings.question_for_authors: How should a reader compare a Cramer's V with a Pearson r in the same sorted spreadsheet?

findings.evidence: Radiomic features are reduced by PCA (10 components) with no random seed and no statement of the PCA implementation or sign convention; component signs therefore cannot be matched across runs.
findings.question_for_authors: Which PCA implementation and sign convention were used for the 10 radiomic components?

findings.evidence: 0 multiply-reported quantities disagree across locations; 5 re-computed values match the paper.
